**Moore bound argument:**

Take any vertex v. Since deg(v) ≥ 5, v has at least 5 neighbors N(v) = {u₁,...,u₅}.

Each uᵢ has degree ≥ 5, so has ≥ 4 neighbors besides v.

For girth ≥ 6:
- No two neighbors of v can be adjacent (would create a 3-cycle)
- No two neighbors of v can share a common neighbor other than v (would create a 4-cycle)
- No neighbor of v can be a neighbor of v's other neighbors-of-neighbors... (checking 5-cycles)

So the neighbors-of-neighbors (excluding v itself) must all be distinct from each other and from N(v).

This gives at least: 1 (for v) + 5 (neighbors) + 5×4 (second neighbors) = **26 vertices required**.

With only 25 vertices, this is impossible.
